
# Project context

Native SwiftUI iPhone client for **Family Central Control**, a self-hosted
household hub (repo: `ryanstephan42/family-task-board`, private). The server is
Express + Prisma + SQLite; this app only talks to it over HTTPS at
`https://<server>/api` with a JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` header).
The API contract is in `docs/API.md`. The authoritative source is the server
code in `server/src/routes/*.ts` of the private repo, which you cannot see:
if a request/response shape is unclear, ask the user for sample JSON rather
than guessing.

## Decisions already made
- SwiftUI, iOS 17+ deployment target (user's phone runs iOS 26.7), no
  third-party dependencies, async/await `URLSession`.
- The user signs with a **free Apple ID** (7-day expiry) on a borrowed Mac and
  upgrades to the paid program later. Do not depend on push notifications,
  App Groups or widgets in v1. Keep signing team and bundle ID changeable
  (`project.yml`; current ID `com.example.familyboard` is a placeholder).
- The Xcode project is generated by XcodeGen (`xcodegen` from `project.yml`);
  do not commit `.xcodeproj`.
- Chat and Budget are out of scope for v1.
- This repo is **public**: never commit secrets, real server domains or tokens.
  Use `family.example.com` in examples and tests. The server address is typed
  into the app at runtime; the token is stored in the Keychain.
- Public repo means free macOS GitHub Actions: add CI that runs XcodeGen,
  builds for the iOS simulator with code signing disabled, and runs unit tests.
  The developer has no always-available Mac, so CI is the main compile check.

## Server facts the app relies on
- Auth: `POST /api/users/login` `{username,password}` -> `{token,user}`.
  Tokens do not expire currently. 401/403 means sign out.
- `GET /api/config` returns `apiVersion` and `minClientApiVersion`; the app
  compares `supportedAPIVersion` (APIClient.swift) and refuses incompatible
  servers.
- Everything except login, register and config needs the JWT.
  `GET /api/users` requires it too.
- Dates are ISO-8601 with fractional seconds (APIClient decodes both forms).
- Uploaded photos are served from `/uploads/...` at the server origin, not
  under `/api`.
- The server sits behind Cloudflare Access with a Bypass policy for `/api/*`
  and `/uploads/*`.
- Uploads (inventory photo field `photo`, receipt field `receipt`) are
  multipart.

## What exists (scaffold)
Server address screen, login, Keychain token, compatibility check, read-only
task list, settings (sign out / change server). See `FamilyBoard/`:
`Services/APIClient.swift`, `Session.swift`, `Keychain.swift`,
`Models/Models.swift`, `Features/`.
It has never been compiled; expect small compile errors to fix first.

## Roadmap (build in this order, one feature per PR)
1. CI workflow (macOS runner, XcodeGen, build + tests) and unit tests for
   URL normalization, date decoding and model decoding.
2. Tasks: create/edit/delete, step checkoff (`PATCH /tasks/:taskId/steps/:stepId`),
   repeating options, assignee picker (`GET /users`), filters (mine, family,
   chores, done via `?status=DONE`).
3. Grocery: list, add (bulk `{items:[...]}`), edit, delete, purchase,
   category grouping, suggestions.
4. Calendar: month and list view, event create and delete.
5. Inventory: list/search, quantity stepper, low stock, add/edit; then photo
   upload and barcode scan (VisionKit `DataScannerViewController`, lookup via
   `/inventory/barcode/:code`).
6. Meals (Mealie-backed) and receipt scan.
7. Offline cache of last-loaded lists; pull-to-refresh, empty/error states.
8. After the paid upgrade: TestFlight, WidgetKit, push.

## Working conventions
- Keep changes small and compile-clean; CI must pass.
- Models mirror `docs/API.md`; mark uncertain fields optional.
- Handle 401/403 centrally by signing out; show server `error` messages.
- Prefer native SwiftUI components, Dynamic Type, dark mode, VoiceOver labels.
